title: HATCH associative boundary-reference retention cross-repository audit
mode: deeper and broader research; plan refinement only
scope: Check DWG HATCH boundary handle counts and handle-stream order against ODA v5.4.1
Compare the DXF per-path association contract with Autodesk documentation and existing libdxfrw model/writer behavior
Use LibreDWG and ezdxf as independent architecture and adversarial-case evidence, not normative authority
Create an implementation-ready PAR-140 / 7N.4 plan while keeping native associative editing separate

authoritativeDwgSpecification.source: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1
sections: §20.4.75 pp.194-197 (per-path count on p.196; flattened handle list on p.197): BL group-97 count is stored per boundary path; after Common Entity Handle Data, the handle stream contains the sum of those per-path counts as H group-330 soft-pointer references.
§2.13 pp.13-15: code 4 is a soft pointer; documented offset encodings 6, 8, A, and C also represent soft-pointer references.
authoritativeDwgSpecification.authority: Normative source for DWG byte layout; exact on-disk text checked with pdftotext and browser-opened official ODA PDF.

dxfSpecification.observed: Group 97 is the number of source boundary objects for a path; repeated group 330 entries reference those objects.

independentImplementations.observed: The release history records a fix for associative-HATCH pattern loss caused by resetting the handle index per path.
independentImplementations.limit: Independent implementation-history evidence only; not DWG format authority or proof of libdxfrw behavior.

independentImplementations.observed: Dwg_HATCH_Path has per-path num_boundary_handles and boundary_handles fields.
independentImplementations.limit: Independent model evidence; no peer binary was built or executed.

independentImplementations.observed: Source boundary handle lists are exposed, but ezdxf states it does not manage or verify the association.
independentImplementations.limit: DXF model/consumer guidance only; not associative-edit or DWG qualification.

independentImplementations.observed: Associative HATCH stores source database-resident objects and can recalculate hatch lines after source edits; per-loop association objects are retrievable.
independentImplementations.limit: Defines why native recompute is a distinct consumer qualification; no native application was run.

observed: DRW_Hatch::parseDwgBoundaryData accumulates only the total boundary-handle count and does not preserve each per-loop count.
DRW_Hatch::parseDwg and DRW_MPolygon::parseDwg consume flattened DWG boundary handles but do not store them in the corresponding DRW_HatchLoop::m_boundaryHandles.
DRW_Hatch::encodeDwgBoundaryData emits a zero boundary-handle count for each loop, even though the loop model and DXF writer support per-loop handles.
The current public m_boundaryHandles type is vector<uint32_t>; dwgHandle retains ref64 as well as a low-32-bit ref, so this path must not silently truncate wider references.

The sibling LibreCAD bundled fork has the same DWG read-discard and write-zero behavior, while retaining per-loop handles and DXF group-97/330 output; an upstream merge alone will not update that vendored route.

The existing --hatch-references ASCII/Binary cases already cover path flags 7/0/2, per-path handle lists {0x31}, {0x32,0x33}, an empty list, and following-entity continuity; they are DXF-only and do not close the DWG gap.

findings.finding: DWG HATCH and MPOLYGON parsing discards per-path associative boundary references, while shared DWG encoding writes zero counts.

smallSlices: Retain one bounded source-boundary-handle count per loop while parsing the path body.
After common entity handles, raw-validate code 4 and documented offset soft-pointer forms 6/8/A/C, resolve values, and partition exactly by the saved per-loop counts.

Reject unsupported reference roles, truncated streams, count overflow, and values wider than the current public 32-bit loop model before callback publication; widen the public representation only if a source-compatible route is designed.
Write each per-loop count and ordered soft-pointer references symmetrically through the correct version-specific handle-buffer placement and end-bound calculations.

Add scratch-only AC1018 and AC1024-or-AC1027 HATCH/MPOLYGON controls with uneven path counts, an empty path, different flags, raw-byte assertions, DXF ASCII/Binary roundtrip, and next-path/entity sentinels.

After the fast codec gate, add one small composed 7F.1 handle-closure control in both DWG→DXF and DXF→DWG directions; refuse before publication if an associative target is dropped or unresolved, without making this closure test a prerequisite for codec-level debugging.
implementationReadiness.fastValidation: Strict focused target build, direct generated selector, and one owning filtered CTest; no full suite until a scheduled composed checkpoint.
implementationReadiness.fixturePolicy: No downloaded or newly committed DWG/DXF fixture; generated data is local, scratch-only, and removed.
implementationReadiness.compatibility: No new pure DRW_Interface virtuals and no change to existing LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 2D callback behavior.
implementationReadiness.bundledLibreCADFork: The sibling bundled fork has the same local loss pattern; track a separate post-review port and consumer compile/readback without editing the sibling in this upstream-only plan pass.
implementationReadiness.semanticBoundary: Reference-field fidelity does not establish target-object existence, geometry/path agreement, or native associative edit/recompute behavior.

focusedVerification.scopeNote: These are existing PAR-115 and DXF path-reference regressions only; no PAR-140 DWG path-reference regression exists yet.
